results.result: T. brucei has a rudimentary actomyosin system with one actin and two myosin genes. TbMyo21 exhibits minimal expression in both BSF and procyclic forms and appears non-essential for BSF growth. TbMyo1 expression is downregulated in procyclic cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C30, C31, and C32 are well-supported by the data. C1 is established knowledge supported by citations. C30 and C31 are demonstrated by immunoblotting (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, 2D) and RNAi growth curves (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F). C32 is supported by immunoblotting (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E) and cited proteomic data, though the authors acknowledge the need for more rigorous controls.

results.result: TbMyo1 is distributed across cytosolic, organelle-associated, and cytoskeleton-associated cellular fractions, with approximately 40% in the cytosolic fraction, 40% in the cytoskeleton-associated fraction, and 57% of gold signals in the cytoplasm by immuno-EM.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C53, and C18 are supported by biochemical fractionation (Figure 1B, 1C) and immuno-electron microscopy (Figure 4I). The fractionation data show ~40% cytosolic and ~40% cytoskeleton-associated TbMyo1, while immuno-EM shows 57% cytoplasmic gold signals. The consistency between methods strengthens the conclusion that TbMyo1 has a substantial cytosolic pool.

results.result: TbMyo1 can translocate actin filaments in vitro at 130 nm/s, which is significantly faster than mammalian class I myosins (10-50 nm/s). TbMyo1 consists of a motor domain, IQ motif, and FYVE domain, and elutes with calmodulin during purification.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C10, C11, and C33 are well-supported. C2 is directly measured in the in vitro gliding assay (Figure 2E). C10 is based on sequence analysis and structural prediction (Figure 2A). C11 is demonstrated by SDS-PAGE (Figure 2C). C33 is supported by the in vitro data and comparative citations. The authors appropriately note that in vitro conditions may not reflect in vivo complexity (C98, C99).

results.result: TbMyo1 localizes to the posterior region between nucleus and kinetoplast, does not substantially overlap with ER (BiP, ρ=0.35) or Golgi (GRASP, ρ=0.30) markers, and shows moderate correlation with lysosome marker p67 (ρ=0.43) but without direct overlap.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C15 and C54-C56 are supported by expansion microscopy (Figure 3A) and colocalisation experiments with correlation analysis (Figure 3B, 3C). The weak correlations with biosynthetic pathway markers and moderate correlation with p67 (without direct overlap) are consistently demonstrated. The authors appropriately discuss the distinction between correlation and co-occurrence (C93-C95).

results.result: TbMyo1 shows visual overlap with endocytic cargo (BSA and transferrin) but weak correlations (ρ=0.17 and 0.20, respectively). TbMyo1 and cargo are present in the same locations (cargo-containing endosomes) but in different proportions.
results.evaluation: Claims C16, C17, C57, C58, and C96 are supported by cargo uptake experiments (Figure 3D, 3E). The apparent paradox of visual overlap with weak correlation is explained by the authors as reflecting topological differences (cargo in lumen vs. TbMyo1 on cytosolic side of membranes) and different proportions. This interpretation is later confirmed by immuno-EM (Figure 4). The distinction between correlation and co-occurrence is appropriately discussed.

results.result: TbMyo1 localizes to glycosomes, with 15% of gold signals at glycosomes in immuno-EM. This localization was previously detected by mass spectrometry and represents an unexpected finding meriting further investigation.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C19, C50, and C104 are supported by immuno-EM (Figure 4E, 4I) and CLEM (Figure 5C, 5D). The glycosomal localization is independently validated by prior proteomic data (Vertommen et al., 2008). The authors appropriately note this as unexpected and requiring further investigation. The finding is consistently observed across multiple imaging modalities.

results.result: TbMyo1 colocalizes with early (TbRab5A) and late (TbRab7) endosome markers but not with recycling endosome marker (TbRab11). 15% of TbMyo1 gold signals were found at endosomes in immuno-EM.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C5, and C20 are supported by colocalisation experiments (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, 1B) and immuno-EM (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). The partial overlap with TbRab5A and TbRab7 but not TbRab11 suggests TbMyo1 functions in post-endocytic trafficking rather than recycling. The correlation coefficients show large variation, consistent with dynamic protein behavior.

results.result: TbMyo1 is clustered adjacent to the lysosome but does not overlap with it. The correlation with lysosome marker p67 is moderate (ρ=0.43) with TbMyo1 signal frequently surrounding p67.
results.evaluation: Claims C21, C15, and C56 are supported by CLEM (Figure 5A, 5B) and widefield/SIM microscopy (Figure 3B, 3C). The consistent observation of TbMyo1 clustering adjacent to but not overlapping with the lysosome across multiple imaging modalities strengthens this conclusion. The moderate correlation with large spread of values is consistent with dynamic association.

results.result: An anti-actin chromobody can be used to visualize actin in T. brucei. The chromobody signal is restricted to the posterior region between nucleus and kinetoplast, matching previously reported actin localization. The distribution pattern is consistent despite cell-to-cell variation in expression level.
results.evaluation: Claims C22, C23, C83, C84, and C85 are supported by successful chromobody expression and localization (Figure 6A, 6B). The localization matches prior reports using anti-actin antibodies (García-Salcedo et al., 2004). The consistency of distribution pattern despite expression variation and lack of effect on TbMyo1 localization validate the approach. This represents the first use of chromobodies in trypanosomatids.

results.result: Treatment with latrunculin A disrupts the chromobody signal in a dose-dependent manner, with 2 μM LatA resulting in strong delocalisation or loss of signal. This validates that the chromobody faithfully reports on filamentous actin distribution.
results.evaluation: Claims C24 and C6 are supported by LatA treatment experiments (Figure 6C). The dose-dependent disruption of the chromobody signal (slight at 0.2 μM, strong at 2 μM) validates that the chromobody specifically binds filamentous actin. This control is essential for interpreting the chromobody localization data.

results.result: TbMyo1 and actin strongly overlap in the posterior part of the cell (ρ=0.63), often up to 1 μm away from the kinetoplast/flagellar pocket. Only a minority of cells show signal adjacent to the kinetoplast, suggesting the actomyosin system is not constitutively present at the flagellar pocket and that actin is highly decorated with TbMyo1.
results.evaluation: Claims C25, C59, C86, C87, C88, and C112 are supported by simultaneous imaging of TbMyo1 and actin chromobody (Figure 6D, 6E, 6F). The strong correlation (ρ=0.63) is the highest observed in the study. The distance from the flagellar pocket and minority of cells with signal near the kinetoplast support the conclusion that the actomyosin system is not constitutively present at the site of endocytosis.

results.result: Latrunculin A treatment results in time-dependent morphological changes (50% of cells after 1 hr), delocalisation of the endosomal marker EP1-GFP, and complete loss of endosomal integrity at early timepoints (≤60 min), with large membrane vesicles filling the space between flagellar pocket and lysosome.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C7, C26, C27, C28, C73, C74, and C75 are supported by LatA treatment experiments using EP1-GFP cells (Figure 7A, 7B, 7C). The time-dependent progression from normal morphology (~85% at 0 hr) to morphological changes (50% at 1 hr) to complete disruption is well-documented. The electron microscopy clearly shows loss of endosomal integrity while preserving other structures.

results.result: After LatA treatment, the Golgi complex structure is preserved, clathrin-coated pits and vesicles continue to form at the flagellar pocket, parasites remain motile, and flagellar pocket enlargement is not observed in most cells during 30-60 min incubation. This demonstrates the specificity of the endosomal phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C29, C62, and C63 are supported by electron microscopy of LatA-treated cells (Figure 7C) and observations in the results section. The preservation of Golgi structure, continued clathrin-mediated endocytosis, maintained motility, and lack of flagellar pocket enlargement demonstrate that the endosomal disruption is specific and not due to general cellular toxicity. These are important controls.

results.result: The actomyosin system is required for maintaining endosomal integrity in T. brucei and primarily functions in post-endocytic trafficking events. The actomyosin system either generates or helps maintain the architecture of the trypanosome endosomal system.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C69, C70, and C72 represent the main conclusions of the study. They are supported by the convergence of multiple lines of evidence: TbMyo1 localization to endosomes (C4, C20), overlap with early/late but not recycling endosome markers (C4, C5), absence from flagellar pocket (C86, C87), and specific loss of endosomal integrity upon LatA treatment (C28, C29). The authors appropriately note that direct functional investigation is still needed (C100, C101).

results.result: TbMyo1 depletion by RNAi causes a penetrant phenotype with most cells rounded after 24 hr. Cells with less deranged morphology can still internalize BSA and traffic it to a lysosome-adjacent compartment. Clathrin-coated vesicles and patches are frequently observed, suggesting endocytosis is not strongly affected.
results.evaluation: Claims C64, C65, and C66 are supported by RNAi experiments (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, 1D). However, the severe morphological phenotype makes interpretation difficult. The authors acknowledge that rounded cells are 'not phenotypically informative' and that only preliminary EM analysis was performed. The conclusion that endocytosis is not strongly affected is tentative. More rigorous analysis is needed to definitively assess the functional role of TbMyo1.

results.result: The large cytosolic fraction of TbMyo1 could indicate auto-inhibited 'foldback' configuration or high turnover dynamics. The relatively high velocity (130 nm/s) suggests TbMyo1 functions as an active motor rather than static tether. The actomyosin system in T. brucei is highly dynamic.
results.evaluation: Claims C67, C97, C68, and C114 are speculative interpretations of the data. C67 and C97 are explicitly stated as speculation requiring testing. C68 is an inference from the in vitro velocity data, but the authors appropriately note that in vivo activities have not been investigated (C99). C114 is inferred from velocity data and cell-to-cell variation (C113). These are reasonable hypotheses but require direct experimental validation.

results.result: This study represents the first use of CLEM on cryosections in trypanosomes, confirming it as a viable experimental approach for T. brucei.
results.evaluation: Claims C123 and C124 are supported by the successful CLEM experiments (Figure 5). The correlation of fluorescence and electron microscopy images demonstrates the technical feasibility of this approach in T. brucei. This is a methodological advance for the field, though it is a minor technical contribution relative to the biological findings.

results.result: TbMyo1 and actin may not be essential for endocytosis to occur. A mechanism similar to mammalian cells, where actin is recruited to endocytic sites primarily when endocytosis stalls, could be at work in trypanosomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C71, C116, and C117 are explicitly stated as speculation in the discussion. The absence of strong signals at the flagellar pocket (C86, C87) and continued presence of clathrin-coated vesicles after LatA treatment (C29, C66) provide some support. However, prior work showed actin depletion causes loss of endocytic activity (C39), which contradicts this speculation. The authors acknowledge this is speculative and requires further investigation.

results.result: The predicted FYVE domain in TbMyo1 is predicted to bind PI(3)P lipids enriched in endosomal membranes. Preliminary unpublished data indicate the FYVE domain can specifically bind PI(3)P. Nothing is known about lipid composition of endosomal membranes in trypanosomes, but expression of FYVE-GFP might be useful to visualize PI(3)P-enriched membranes.
results.evaluation: Claims C46, C47, C102, and C103 involve predictions and preliminary unpublished data. C46 is a reasonable prediction based on FYVE domain function in other organisms. C47 cites unpublished observations that cannot be evaluated. C102 acknowledges the lack of knowledge about trypanosome endosomal lipid composition. C103 is speculation about future experiments. These claims require publication of the preliminary data and direct experimental validation.

results.result: The close juxtaposition of ERES and Golgi in T. brucei could explain why TbMyo1 might be dispensable for transport between these organelles. Secretory material might move in bulk from Golgi to the endosomal system, which serves as a central sorting hub for both secretory and endocytic cargo.
results.evaluation: Claims C90, C91, and C92 are speculative interpretations based on the lack of TbMyo1 association with biosynthetic pathway markers (C13, C14) and cited models. C90 and C91 are supported by citations but represent speculation about mechanisms not directly tested in this study. C92 is part of a proposed model. These are reasonable hypotheses consistent with the data but require direct experimental validation.

results.result: TbMyo21 is unlikely to be a viable drug target in T. brucei due to low expression and non-essential role. The discrepancy in TbMyo1 expression between BSF and PCF compared to prior studies is likely due to improved antibodies, though more rigorous controls are needed. The actomyosin system may be less critical for procyclic cells with lower membrane trafficking rates.
results.evaluation: Claims C118, C119, C120, and C121 are supported by the expression and RNAi data (Figure 1—figure supplement 2). C118 is a reasonable inference from C30 and C31. C119 and C120 appropriately acknowledge limitations in the comparison to prior work. C121 is a reasonable inference from C32 and known differences in membrane trafficking between life stages. The authors appropriately note the need for more rigorous controls.

results.result: TbMyo1 can translocate actin filaments in vitro at a velocity of 130 nm/s, which is significantly faster than mammalian class I myosins (10-50 nm/s), suggesting TbMyo1 functions as an active motor rather than a static tether in intracellular trafficking.
results.evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. Reviewer 2 states the study 'demonstrates that TbMyo1 can translocate actin filaments at velocities suggesting an active role in intracellular trafficking, potentially higher than those observed for similar myosins in other cell types.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the authors have shown that the T. brucei Myo1 homolog is a dynamic motor that can translocate actin, suggesting that it may not function as a more passive crosslinker.' No concerns are raised about the in vitro motility data or velocity measurements.

results.result: TbMyo1 has a large cytosolic pool (~40-57% in different fractionation methods), with the remaining portion partitioning into cytoskeleton-associated and organellar fractions.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the biochemical fractionation data without challenge. Reviewer 1 notes 'a great part of the myosin motor is cytoplasmic but the fraction associated with organelles is in proximity to the endosomal system and in glycosomes.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'TbMyo1 is dynamically distributed across early and late endosomes, the cytosol, is associated with the cytoskeleton.' The quantification and distribution are not questioned.

results.result: TbMyo1 localizes to the endosomal system, colocalizing with early and late endosome markers (TbRab5A and TbRab7) but not recycling endosomes (TbRab11), and is found in close proximity to lysosomes and endocytic cargo (BSA and transferrin).
results.evaluation: All reviewers affirm the endosomal localization findings. The editor states the study 'present[s] compelling evidence that an actomyosin system, with the myosin TbMyo1 as an active molecular motor, is localized close to and can associate with the endosomal system.' Reviewer 3 confirms 'MyoI localizes to the endosomal pathway, specifically the portion tasked with internalizing and targeting cargo for degradation, not the recycling endosomes.' The colocalisation data and correlation analyses are accepted without critique.

results.result: TbMyo1 localizes to glycosomes, with 15% of gold signals found at glycosomes in immuno-EM experiments, representing an unexpected finding that merits further investigation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly highlight this as a novel and important finding. Reviewer 2 states 'the discovery of TbMyo1 localization to glycosomes introduces a novel aspect to the potential roles of myosin I proteins within the cell, particularly in the context of organelles analogous to peroxisomes. This observation not only broadens our understanding of myosin I functionality but also opens up new avenues for research.' Reviewer 3 notes 'The glycosomes also appear to be associated with MyoI, which was previously not known.' No concerns are raised about the glycosome localization data.

results.result: An anti-actin chromobody can visualize actin in T. brucei, showing signal restricted to the posterior region between nucleus and kinetoplast that strongly overlaps with TbMyo1 (correlation ρ = 0.63) and is disrupted by latrunculin A treatment.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the chromobody approach and actin-TbMyo1 colocalization. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'visualize for the first time this actomyosin system using specific antibodies, a "classical" antibody for TbMyo1, and a chromobody for actin.' Reviewer 3 notes 'An actin chromobody was employed to determine the localization of filamentous actin in cells, which was correlated with the localization of Myo1.' The strong correlation and latrunculin A sensitivity are accepted without challenge.

results.result: Disruption of the actomyosin system using latrunculin A results in delocalisation of actin and endosomal markers, accompanied by specific loss of endosomal structure while preserving Golgi structure and clathrin-coated vesicles, demonstrating that the actomyosin system is required for maintaining endosomal integrity.
results.evaluation: All reviewers strongly support this central conclusion. The editor states the study 'shows convincingly that both actin and Myo I play a role in the organization and integrity of the endosomal system: both RNAi-mediated depletion of Myo1, and treatment of the cells with latrunculin A resulted in endomembrane disruption.' Reviewer 1 confirms 'using latrunculin A, which sequesters G-actin and prevents F-actin assembly, the authors show the delocalization and eventually the loss of the filamentous actin signal and the concomitant loss of the endosomal system integrity.' Reviewer 3 states 'the authors used actin-perturbing drugs to show that disrupting actin causes a collapse of the endosomal system.' The specificity of the phenotype is noted and accepted.

results.result: RNAi-mediated depletion of TbMyo1 causes a penetrant phenotype with cell rounding after 24 hours, but cells with less deranged morphology can still internalize BSA and traffic it to lysosome-adjacent compartments, with clathrin-coated vesicles still present, suggesting endocytosis is not strongly affected.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as addressing a previous weakness. Reviewer 2 states 'A significant initial weakness was the reliance on spatial association data to infer functional relationships without direct demonstration of biochemical activities in vivo. The authors have since addressed this by including new evidence from TbMyo1 RNAi cell lines and EM data that show the effects of TbMyo1 depletion on cellular ultrastructure.' Reviewer 3 notes 'The revised manuscript has addressed the main issue, the lack of TbMyo1 functional data that was brought up during the first round of review. I find it interesting that Myo1 depletion has what appears to be a limited effect on endocytosis while producing a similar fragmentation of the endocytic pathway to what is seen with the LatA treatments. As CCV remains in both LatA treatments and TbMyo1 RNAi, it seems apparent that the organization of the endocytic pathway is not required for at least basal levels of endocytosis.'

results.result: TbMyo1 does not substantially overlap with ER (BiP) or Golgi (GRASP) markers, showing weak correlations (ρ = 0.35 and 0.30 respectively).
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these negative localization findings without challenge. The data support the specificity of TbMyo1's endosomal localization by excluding other organelles. No concerns are raised about the correlation analyses or interpretation.

results.result: TbMyo21 exhibits minimal expression in both BSF and procyclic form cells and appears to be non-essential for BSF cell growth based on RNAi experiments.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings about TbMyo21 without challenge. The low expression and non-essential nature are presented as supporting data explaining the focus on TbMyo1. No concerns are raised about the expression or RNAi data for TbMyo21.

results.result: TbMyo1 expression is downregulated in the procyclic life cycle stage, suggesting the actomyosin system is not as critical for procyclic cells which have lower membrane trafficking rates than BSF cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding without challenge. The downregulation in PCF is presented as consistent with proteomic data and the lower trafficking demands of this life stage. No concerns are raised about the expression data or interpretation.

results.result: TbMyo1 is predicted to consist of a motor domain, IQ motif, and FYVE domain that can bind PI(3)P lipids, with TbMyo1 eluting together with calmodulin during size-exclusion chromatography.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the structural predictions and biochemical characterization. Reviewer 2 notes the study uses 'biochemical fractionation, in vitro motility assays, and advanced imaging techniques' comprehensively. The FYVE domain prediction and preliminary PI(3)P binding data are accepted as supporting the membrane association model. No concerns are raised about the structural analysis or calmodulin binding.

results.result: Even after 30-60 min of latrunculin A incubation causing complete endosomal disruption, parasites remain motile and flagellar pocket enlargement is not observed in most cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these observations as demonstrating the specificity of the endosomal phenotype. The preservation of motility and flagellar pocket structure supports that the effects are specific to the endosomal system rather than global cellular dysfunction. No concerns are raised about these observations.

results.result: The actomyosin system is often located up to 1 μm away from the kinetoplast/flagellar pocket region, with only a minority of cells showing signals adjacent to the kinetoplast, suggesting the actomyosin system is not constitutively present at the flagellar pocket and primarily functions in post-endocytic trafficking events rather than being essential for endocytosis itself.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this interpretation of the localization data. Reviewer 3 notes 'Interestingly, the pool of actomyosin was not always closely associated with the flagellar pocket region, suggesting that portions of the endolysomal system may remain at a distance from the sole site of parasite endocytosis.' The conclusion that actomyosin functions post-endocytosis is supported by the RNAi and LatA data showing continued endocytosis despite endosomal disruption. No challenges to this interpretation are raised.

results.result: This study represents the first use of CLEM on cryosections in trypanosomes, confirming it as a viable experimental approach for T. brucei.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praise the technical achievements. Reviewer 2 states 'A key strength of the study is its exceptional rigor and successful integration of a wide array of sophisticated techniques, such as in vitro motility assays, and advanced imaging methods, e.g. CLEM.' The successful application of CLEM is accepted as a methodological advance. No concerns are raised about the CLEM approach or data quality.

results.result: The actomyosin system either generates or helps maintain the architecture of the trypanosome endosomal system, with the primary focus and function of trypanosome actin and TbMyo1 centered on the endosomal system, which serves as a central sorting hub for both secretory and endocytic cargo.
results.evaluation: Reviewers support this as the main conclusion of the study. The editor states this work demonstrates 'the actomyosin system is required for maintaining endosomal integrity in T. brucei.' Reviewer 1 confirms the study 'paves the way toward the elucidation of the role of an actomyosin system in the maintenance of the endosomal network.' Reviewer 3 states 'The main premise, that actomyosin is essential for the overall structure of the T. brucei endocytic system, is well supported.' The model of the endosomal system as a central hub is accepted as consistent with the data.

results.result: This study has not rigorously investigated a direct functional role for TbMyo1 in endomembrane function, and further experiments using the TbMyo1 RNAi cell line will be needed to explore this in more detail.
results.evaluation: While reviewers acknowledge the authors' caveat about functional mechanisms, Reviewer 1 notes 'Although disruption of the actomyosin system using either the actin-depolymerizing drug latrunculin A or the TbMyo1-RNAi cell line established an effect on the endosomal system integrity, it remains to understand how this occurs mechanistically and what are the intracellular components involved.' Reviewer 2 states 'Several new, elegant hypotheses are proposed in the discussion that warrant further investigation to fully understand TbMyo1's interactions and regulatory mechanisms in vivo.' This indicates the mechanistic details remain to be fully elucidated despite the functional data provided.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on TbMyo1's cytosolic distribution (C3, C18, C53). Both accept the biochemical fractionation data showing ~40% cytosolic and ~40% cytoskeleton-associated TbMyo1. OpenEval notes consistency with immuno-EM data; peer reviewers accept the quantification without challenge.

Perfect agreement on glycosomal localization (C9, C19, C50, C104). Both recognize this as a novel and unexpected finding. OpenEval notes validation by proteomic data and multiple imaging modalities; peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as opening new research avenues for myosin I functionality.

Agreement on TbMyo1 RNAi findings (C64, C65, C66), but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to severe morphological phenotype making interpretation difficult and acknowledges preliminary nature. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing the RNAi data as successfully addressing a previous weakness and finding the limited effect on endocytosis interesting.

Perfect agreement on CLEM technical achievement (C123, C124). Both recognize this as a methodological advance for the field. OpenEval notes it as a minor technical contribution; peer reviewers explicitly praise the exceptional rigor and successful integration of sophisticated techniques.

Agreement on specificity controls (C62, C63, C29). Both accept that preservation of Golgi, motility, and flagellar pocket structure demonstrates the endosomal disruption is specific. OpenEval emphasizes these as important controls; peer reviewers accept them as demonstrating specificity of the phenotype.

Agreement on negative localization findings (C13, C14, C54, C55). Both accept the weak correlations with biosynthetic pathway markers. OpenEval notes appropriate discussion of correlation vs. co-occurrence; peer reviewers accept these findings as supporting the specificity of TbMyo1's endosomal localization.

Agreement on TbMyo21 findings (C30, C31). Both accept the low expression and non-essential nature of TbMyo21. OpenEval also addresses C1 and C32 (TbMyo1 expression and PCF downregulation); peer reviewers focus only on TbMyo21 data as supporting the focus on TbMyo1.

Strong agreement on latrunculin A effects (C6, C7, C26, C27, C28). Both accept the time-dependent disruption of endosomal integrity and specificity of the phenotype. OpenEval emphasizes the progression and EM documentation; peer reviewers strongly support this as a central conclusion showing actomyosin's role in endosomal organization.

Agreement on in vitro motility findings (C2, C33). Both accept the velocity measurements and motor activity. OpenEval also addresses C10 and C11 (structural features); peer reviewers explicitly affirm TbMyo1 as a dynamic motor suggesting active role in trafficking, potentially higher velocities than similar myosins.

Agreement on main conclusions (C8, C69, C70, C72) but with nuance. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting convergence of evidence while acknowledging need for direct functional investigation. Peer reviewers also support the main premise but note (R16) that mechanistic details remain to be elucidated despite functional data provided.

Agreement on endosomal localization (C4, C5, C20). Both accept colocalisation with Rab5A/Rab7 but not Rab11, indicating post-endocytic trafficking. OpenEval emphasizes multiple imaging modalities; peer reviewers affirm compelling evidence for actomyosin localization to endosomal system, also noting C12, C15, C16, C17, C21.

Agreement on actomyosin localization relative to flagellar pocket (C86, C87, C88). Both accept that TbMyo1 is not constitutively present at the site of endocytosis. OpenEval notes strong correlation with actin and distance from flagellar pocket; peer reviewers accept this supports post-endocytic function, also addressing C69 and C71.

Agreement on structural features (C10, C11). Both accept sequence analysis, structural predictions, and protein purification. OpenEval emphasizes SDS-PAGE validation; peer reviewers accept structural predictions and biochemical characterization as part of comprehensive approach, also addressing C46 and C47 (FYVE domain).

Agreement on FYVE domain predictions (C46, C47). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to unpublished preliminary data requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the FYVE domain prediction and preliminary PI(3)P binding data as supporting the membrane association model.

Agreement on chromobody approach (C22, C23). Both accept successful chromobody expression and validation. OpenEval emphasizes this as first use in trypanosomatids and consistency with prior reports; peer reviewers affirm visualization of actomyosin system for the first time, also addressing C24, C25, C59 (LatA sensitivity and colocalization).

Partial overlap on endosomal localization. OpenEval R8 focuses on TbMyo1 clustering adjacent to lysosome (C21, C15, C56); peer R3 addresses broader endosomal localization including C4, C5, C12, C15, C16, C17, C20, C21. Both support the endosomal association findings.

Partial overlap on actin-TbMyo1 colocalization. OpenEval R11 emphasizes strong correlation (C25, C59, C86, C87, C88, C112); peer R5 focuses on chromobody validation and colocalization (C22, C23, C24, C25, C59). Both support the actomyosin colocalization findings.

Partial overlap on TbMyo1 expression. OpenEval R1 addresses multiple expression claims (C1, C30, C31, C32); peer R10 focuses specifically on PCF downregulation (C32, C121). Both accept the expression data and life stage differences.

Minimal overlap on biosynthetic pathway interpretation. OpenEval R20 rates speculation about biosynthetic vs. degradative pathways (C90, C91, C92) as UNCERTAIN; peer R15 accepts the model of endosomal system as central hub (C70, C72, C92) as SUPPORTED main conclusion.

Minimal overlap on life stage differences. OpenEval R21 addresses multiple expression and comparison claims (C118, C119, C120, C121); peer R10 focuses on PCF downregulation (C32, C121). Both accept the life stage expression differences.

Minimal overlap on cargo uptake and endosomal localization. OpenEval R5 focuses on cargo uptake experiments and correlation vs. co-occurrence (C16, C17, C57, C58, C96); peer R3 addresses broader endosomal localization. Both support endosomal association but emphasize different aspects.

Minimal overlap on latrunculin A validation. OpenEval R10 focuses on LatA validation of chromobody specificity (C24, C6); peer R5 addresses chromobody approach more broadly (C22, C23, C24, C25, C59). Both accept LatA sensitivity as validating the actin detection.

Minimal overlap on velocity interpretation. OpenEval R16 rates speculation about in vivo velocity and regulation (C67, C97, C68, C114) as UNCERTAIN; peer R1 accepts in vitro velocity findings (C2, C33, C68) as SUPPORTED, affirming active role in trafficking.

Minimal overlap on endocytosis mechanism. OpenEval R18 rates speculation about actomyosin not being required for endocytosis itself (C71, C116, C117) as UNCERTAIN; peer R13 accepts that actomyosin functions post-endocytosis (C86, C87, C88, C69, C71) as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on actin disruption. OpenEval R10 focuses on chromobody validation with LatA (C24, C6); peer R6 focuses on endosomal disruption phenotype with LatA (C6, C7, C8, C26, C27, C28, C29). Both involve LatA but address different aspects.

Minimal overlap on post-endocytic function. OpenEval R14 addresses main conclusions about endosomal integrity (C8, C69, C70, C72); peer R13 focuses on localization away from flagellar pocket supporting post-endocytic function (C86, C87, C88, C69, C71). Both support post-endocytic role.

Minimal overlap on specificity of phenotype. OpenEval R13 focuses on preservation of other structures as controls (C29, C62, C63); peer R6 emphasizes the endosomal disruption phenotype itself (C6, C7, C8, C26, C27, C28, C29). Both address LatA effects but different aspects.

Minimal overlap on endosomal integrity conclusion. OpenEval R14 addresses main conclusions (C8, C69, C70, C72); peer R6 focuses on LatA-induced disruption (C6, C7, C8, C26, C27, C28, C29). Both support role in endosomal integrity but emphasize different evidence.

Both address need for mechanistic understanding (C100, C101).
